import mir_eval

# Ensure inputs are (n, 2) and (m, 2) intervals, slicing off any pitch/velocity columns
ref_ints = ref_intervals[:, :2]
est_ints = est_intervals[:, :2]

# Call the function with default (strict=False) and strict=True
matching = mir_eval.transcription.match_note_onsets(ref_ints, est_ints, onset_tolerance=0.05, strict=False)
matching_strict = mir_eval.transcription.match_note_onsets(ref_ints, est_ints, onset_tolerance=0.05, strict=True)

# Verify the output type and basic bounds
assert isinstance(matching, list), "Matching should be a list of tuples"
assert len(matching) <= min(len(ref_ints), len(est_ints)), "Cannot have more matches than notes"
assert len(matching_strict) <= len(matching), "Strict matching should yield subset or equal number of matches"

# Verify the onset tolerance constraint for non-strict matching
for i, j in matching:
    onset_diff = abs(ref_ints[i, 0] - est_ints[j, 0])
    assert onset_diff <= 0.05 + 1e-9, f"Matched onsets {i} and {j} exceed tolerance: {onset_diff}"

# Verify the onset tolerance constraint for strict matching
for i, j in matching_strict:
    onset_diff = abs(ref_ints[i, 0] - est_ints[j, 0])
    assert onset_diff < 0.05, f"Strict matched onsets {i} and {j} exceed or equal tolerance: {onset_diff}"

# Verify that every reference and estimated note is matched at most once (bipartite matching property)
ref_matched = set(i for i, j in matching)
est_matched = set(j for i, j in matching)
assert len(ref_matched) == len(matching), "A reference note was matched multiple times"
assert len(est_matched) == len(matching), "An estimated note was matched multiple times"

print(f"__CHECK__ match_note_onsets {len(matching)}")
